rounds.text: Yuranus Infrastructure Ltd demonstrates exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 200% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 279% [E16, E21]. Operational efficiency is scaling rapidly, with the TTM operating margin expanding to 12% from 3% three years prior, and quarterly operating margin reaching 14% in Sep 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, profitability metrics compare favourably against sector benchmarks, including an ROA of 10.07% versus the sector 4.74% and an ROCE of 13% [E8, E10]. Valuation disconnect provides a compelling entry angle, as a discounted cash flow valuation yields an intrinsic value of Rs 234 per share against a market price of Rs 100, offering a 57.2% margin of safety [E43, E44]. Adding institutional backing to this growth story, foreign institutions have increased their stake by 5.10% since December 2023 to reach 5.10% by September 2026 [E41]. Conceded: price-to-book sits at an elevated 9.52x against a book value of ₹ 10.5 [E2].

The valuation is detached from sector norms, with the price-to-earnings ratio sitting at 48.69x against a sector benchmark of 14.04x [E6], and the price-to-book ratio reaching 9.51x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.23x [E7]. Profit growth fails to translate into actual liquidity, as demonstrated by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.06x for March 2026, where reported profits vastly outpace operating cash flows of Rs 0.03 Cr and result in a negative free cash flow of Rs -0.02 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. Operational efficiency is deteriorating underneath the top-line growth, evidenced by debtor days expanding from 37.7 to 83.1 days and working capital days surging from 39.8 to 86.5 days [E51, E52]. Historical returns remain modest rather than stellar, highlighted by a 10-year median return on equity of only 7% and a current ROE of 9.0% [E13, E26]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has accelerated significantly over recent periods, reaching 111% in the trailing twelve months and 200% over 3 years [E16, E17].

Conceded: the sector comparisons show higher valuation multiples [E6, E7], and debtor and working capital days have indeed expanded [E51, E52]. However, the bear's focus on historical ROE overlooks current fundamental strength, such as an ROA of 10.07% beating the sector benchmark of 4.74% [E8], and a ROCE of 13% aligning closely with the sector [E10]. While cash conversion reads low for the single period of March 2026 [E34], borrowings actively decreased over that exact timeframe from Rs 2.10 Cr to Rs 1.89 Cr, showing prudent balance sheet management [E38]. Furthermore, the bear's dismissal of top-line expansion understates a massive turnaround: compounded profit growth reached 279% in the trailing twelve months [E21], and quarterly operating margin surged by 31 percentage points year-over-year [E31]. Finally, foreign institutional investors have recognized this operational momentum, increasing their holding from 0.00% to 5.10% [E41].

Conceded: foreign institutional holdings increased to 5.10% [E41]. However, citing an ROA of 10.07% [E8] or a ROCE of 13% [E10] ignores the company's multi-year median ROE of just 7% over 10 years [E26] and its low 3-year average ROE of 13.5% [E50]. The claim that debt reduction proves prudent management [E38] is directly undermined by a cash conversion ratio of 0.06x, which flags that reported profits are entirely disconnected from actual cash generation and point to problematic receivables [E34]. That severe cash disconnect is corroborated by debtor days ballooning from 37.7 to 83.1 days and working capital days surging to 86.5 days [E51, E52], creating a severe liquidity risk that makes the negative free cash flow of Rs -0.02 Cr [E36] unsurprising. Finally, celebrating a 279% profit spike [E21] or a quarterly margin surge [E31] ignores the official flag that the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are strictly inconsistent [E32, E33], proving these momentum spikes are erratic rather than durable.
